newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam president still critical after stroke.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam president still critical after stroke.

text.p: Vietnam's President Le Duc Anh remained in critical condition on Tuesday after suffering a stroke and is unlikely to recover sufficiently to resume his presidential duties, political and diplomatic sources said.
The communist government on Monday broke its silence over the 75-year-old general's health, but said only that he was tired and in need of rest.

But sources said Anh, a member of the ruling triumvirate of septuagenarian leaders, had been paralysed on one side of his body by the stroke and remained under close observation in Hanoi's 108 Military Hospital.
"It's very serious," said one diplomat. "For sure, he will be replaced."

Political sources said discussion of what steps to take in the light of Anh's incapacitation would probably get under way once South Korean President Kim Young-sam, who arrives in Vietnam on Wednesday, leaves after a two-day visit.
Although he has a behind-the-scenes role, the president is an important figure in Vietnam because he is in charge of foreign policy, defence and internal security of the Communist Party.
Under the constitution, when the president is incapacitated "over a long period of time" the vice president must act in his place.

The sources said that while Vice President Nguyen Thi Binh may stand in temporarily, she would not be expected to take over. If the post is declared vacant, a new president would have to be elected by the National Assembly.

Anh is viewed by Western observers as the most conservative of the leadership troika, a collective system comprising powerful figures chosen to ensure balance between different shades of socialist opinion and differing regional views.
The other members of the troika are Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi, who is seen as occupying a central and stabilising role in government, and the reformist Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet.
